monument_name: Dharma Gaddi statues and stone memorial pillar
context: Of note are a few Buddhist deities: a broken Buddha (DLK0200-003), a Saḍakṣarī Lokeśvara (?, (DLK0200-002), and the bust of a potential Avalokiteśvara (DLK0200-007). Another sculpture, also identified as Avalokiteśvara is placed in a niche (DLK0200-005). The face of the figure, seated on a column in a "royal position of ease", has been deliberately damaged. All the Buddhist sculptures show signs of iconoclastic vandalism. The condition of the so-called Avalokiteśvara bust and the Avalokiteśvara seated on the column would therefore tend to identify them as Buddhist figures. The presence of Buddhism in this place is also attested by an inscribed but illegible stele decorated with an incised stūpa at the top (DLK0200-001). A stele of Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī, meanwhile, shows no marks of vandalism (Andolfatto 2019: p. 166). According to P. R. Sharma the so-called bust of Avalokiteśvara (DLK0200-007) was installed (in 1967) in "Dullu Bhairavathan", which is a small temple south of Dharma Gaddi (Sharma 1972: p. 28). D. R. Sharma proposes to date this sculpture from the 11th century (Sharma 2012: p. 40).The artefacts may be roughly dated from the 12th to the 19th century.
